1.why: All eight screenshots show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary headings, teal action buttons, and yellow phishing callouts are visually distinct from body text.

3.why: Numbered step labels and a single prominent form per screen make the required action easy to locate.

4.why: The flow spans six mandatory steps and requires recalling complex password composition rules and one-time tokens.

5.why: No password-manager affordance, autofill prompt, or “remember me” control appears on any screen.

6.why: The recovery screens present only empty fields; no previously saved addresses or familiar account cues are shown.

7.why: Instructional sentences are brief, use plain language, and avoid dense paragraphs.

8.why: No error states or error messages are present in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: A sample MFA code is displayed in step 3, yet password and token fields lack input examples.

10.why: The UI offers only password-plus-code entry; no alternative methods such as face login are presented as choices.

11.why: Each step contains at most two input fields and a single primary button, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Step titles advance, confirmation pages appear, and the final green banner explicitly states the appointment request outcome.

13.why: Phishing tips and password-rule text appear, but contextual help or tooltips for each new step are otherwise absent.

14.why: No back, retry, or edit controls are visible; the only related note mentions lock-out after repeated failures.

15.why: Every screen re-uses the same header, card layout, button style, and log panel, maintaining visual consistency.
